Erste Abtheilung: Plakoiden und Pyknodonten |journal=Abhandlungen der Mathemat.-physikalischen Classe der Königlich Bayerischen Akademie der Wissenschaften |volume=9 |issue=2 |pages=277–352 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/35523290#page/321/mode/1up}} * ''[[Hexanchus]] wagneri''
(Agassiz, 1843){{cite journal |last=Fowler |first=H.W. |date=1967 |title=A catalog of world fishes (VI) |journal=Quarterly Journal of the Taiwan Museum |volume=20 |issue=1–2 |pages=79–148}}}} }} }} '''''Georgaello''''' is an extinct [[genus]] of [[Neoselachii|neoselachians]] that lived during the [[Late Jurassic]]. It contains two species, '''''G''. ''elongata''''' and '''''G''. ''wagneri''''', which have been found in [[Germany]]. ==Taxonomy== ''Aellopos elongata'' was named by [[Georg zu Münster]] in 1836 for a partial holomorphic specimen, a posterior body with [[Dorsal fin|dorsal]] and [[Fish fin#AnchCaudal|caudal]] (and possibly other) fins,{{efn|Other sources have claimed that [[Pelvic fin|pelvic]] and/or [[Fish fin#AnchPectoral|pectoral]] and [[Fish fin#AnchAnal|anal]]{{cite journal |last=Reis |first=O.M. |date=1893 |title=Untersuchungen über die Petrificirung der Muskulatur |journal=Archiv für Mikroskopische Anatomie |volume=41 |pages=492–584 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/49524#page/502/mode/1up |doi=10.1007/bf02954332}} fins are also present in this specimen.}} from the [[Kelheim]] locality in Germany. ''Aellopos wagneri'' was named by [[Louis Agassiz]] in 1843 for another partial holomorphic specimen, essentially the same parts as ''A''. ''elongata'', apparently from the [[Solnhofen]] locality in Germany.{{efn|Other sources have claimed that this specimen originated from the [[Pappenheim]]{{cite journal |last=Wagner |first=R. |date=1829 |title=Nachrichten von der Petrefactensammlung der Königlichen Academie der Wissenschaften in München |journal=Archiv für die gesammte Naturlehre |volume=16 |issue=1 |pages=71–96 |url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=hvd.hw2b7b&seq=87}} or [[Eichstätt]]{{cite book |last=Hasse |first=C. |date=1882 |title=Das natürliche System der Elasmobranchier auf Grundlage des Baues und der Entwicklung ihrer Wirbelsäule. Eine morphologische und paläontologische Studie. Besonderer Theil |location=Jena, DE |publisher=Gustav Fischer |doi=10.5962/bhl.title.8431 |doi-access=free |pages=[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/34919#page/198/mode/1up 104-108] [https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/35007#page/77/mode/1up 13-14]}} localities.}} The [[holotype]]s of both species are housed at the [[Palaeontological Museum, Munich|Bayerische Staatssammlung für Paläontologie und Geologie]]; either of them may or may not be the specimen catalogued as SNSB-BSPG AS VII 1170.{{Cite journal |last1=Türtscher |first1=J. |last2=Jambura |first2=P.L. |last3=Villalobos-Segura |first3=E. |last4=López-Romero |first4=F.A. |last5=Underwood |first5=C.J. |last6=Thies |first6=D. |last7=Lauer |first7=B. |last8=Lauer |first8=R. |last9=Kriwet |first9=J. |date=2024 |title=Rostral and body shape analyses reveal cryptic diversity of Late Jurassic batomorphs (Chondrichthyes, Elasmobranchii) from Europe |journal=Papers in Palaeontology |volume=10 |issue=2 |article-number=e1552 |doi=10.1002/spp2.1552 |pmid=38799546 |pmc=7615989 |bibcode=2024PPal...10E1552T }} Additionally, some [[Fish_anatomy#Vertebrae|vertebrae]] were later extracted from the ''A''. ''elongata'' holotype and possibly taken to the [[University of Wrocław|Uniwersytet Wrocławski]]. The [[Basionym|original]] genus name is [[Homonym (biology)|preoccupied]] by the lepidopteran ''[[Aellopos]]'' named by [[Jacob Hübner]] in 1819. In 1846, Agassiz proposed the [[Emendation (zoology)|unjustified]], but [[Available name|available]], emendation ''Aellopus''. However, this name is preoccupied by the hemipteran ''[[Aellopus atratus|Aellopus]]'' named by {{ill|Johann Philipp Wolff|lt=Johann P. Wolff|de|Johann Philipp Wolff (Mediziner, 1747)}} in 1811. The [[Available name#Unavailable names|unavailable]], [[incorrect subsequent spelling]]s ''Aelopos'' and ''Allopos'' were used by [[Christoph Gottfried Andreas Giebel|Christoph Giebel]] in 1846 and [[Henry Weed Fowler|Henry W. Fowler]] in 1911, respectively. ''A''. ''wagneri'' was also formerly considered a species of ''[[Hexanchus|Notidanus]]'' or ''[[Hexanchus]]'' but is not actually assignable to them. Since none of the aforementioned genera can be applied, ''Georgaello'' was named as a [[Nomen novum|replacement]] in 2026. ''G''. ''wagneri'' was the first [[Chondrichthyes|chondrichthyan]] recognized from the [[Solnhofen Limestone]], while ''G''. ''elongata'' was one of the first named as a distinct genus and species. The former was briefly described as ''[[Spurdog|Squalus]]'' by [[Rudolf Wagner]] in 1829 and the latter was named the same year as ''[[Asterodermus|Asterodermus platypterus]]''.{{cite book |last=Agassiz |first=J.L.R. |date=1835–1843 |title=Recherches sur les poissons fossiles. Tome III. Atlas |location=Neuchâtel, CH |publisher=H. Nicolet |doi=10.5962/bhl.title.4275 |doi-access=free |page=[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/99978#page/85/mode/1up 44]}} Both species were redescribed by [[Johann Andreas Wagner|Johann A. Wagner]] in 1861, and ''G''. ''elongata'' by {{ill|Carl Hasse|lt=Carl Hasse|de|Carl Hasse}} in 1882 and {{ill|Otto Maria Reis|lt=Otto M. Reis|de|Otto Maria Reis}} in 1893. ==Classification== The species of ''Georgaello'' were previously considered similar to and/or synonymous with several chondrichthyans from the Late Jurassic of [[Europe]], including ''[[Pseudorhina|Pseudorhina acanthoderma]]'', ''[[Crassodontidanidae|Notidanoides muensteri]]'',{{cite book |last=Quenstedt |first=F.A. |date=1865–1866 |title=Handbuch der Petrefaktenkunde. Zweite umgearbeitete und vermehrte Auflage |location=Tübingen, DE |publisher=H. Laupp |pages=[https://www.google.com/books/edition/_/VTvPAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&pg=PA205 205-206]}} ''[[Spathobatis|Spathobatis bugesiaca]]'',{{cite book |last=Woodward |first=A.S. |date=1889 |title=Catalogue of the Fossil Fishes in the British Museum (Natural History), Cromwell Road, S.W. Part I. Containing the Elasmobranchii |location=London, GB |publisher=Trustees of the British Museum |doi=10.5962/bhl.title.161983 |doi-access=free |page=[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/271005#page/260/mode/1up 78]}} ''[[Orthacodontidae|Archaeogracilidens macer]]'', and ''[[Aellopobatis|Aellopobatis bavarica]]''. They have also been compared with extant genera such as ''[[Galeorhinus]]'', and ''[[Pristis]]'' and ''[[Pristiophorus]]''. Currently, the classification of ''Georgaello'' cannot be narrowed down past Neoselachii due to a lack of illustrations of the entire holotypes, uncertainty over which museum specimens the holotypes correspond to, and conflicting descriptions of the anatomy. The figured vertebrae of ''G''. ''elongata'' have a tectospondylic calcification pattern like those of ''Pseudorhina'' spp.{{cite book |last1=Carvalho |first1=M.R.d. |last2=Kriwet |first2=J. |last3=Thies |first3=D. |date=2008 |chapter=A systematic and anatomical revision of Late Jurassic angelsharks (Chondrichthyes: Squatinidae) |editor-last1=Arratia |editor-first1=G. |editor-last2=Schultze |editor-first2=H.-P. |editor-last3=Wilson |editor-first3=M.V.H. |title=Mesozoic Fishes 4 – Homology and Phylogeny |location=Munich, DE |publisher=Verlag Dr. Friedrich Pfeil |pages=469–502}} and ''Notidanoides muensteri''.{{cite journal |last1=Kriwet |first1=J. |last2=Klug |first2=S. |date=2014 |title=Dental patterns of the stem-group hexanchoid shark, ''Notidanoides muensteri'' (Elasmobranchii, Hexanchiformes) |journal=Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology |volume=34 |issue=6 |pages=1292–1306 |doi=10.1080/02724634.2014.874353 |bibcode=2014JVPal..34.1292K }} The figured [[Fish scale#Placoid scales|dermal denticles]] match morphotypes found in ''Asterodermus platypterus'', ''Pseudorhina alifera'', ''[[Phorcynis|Phorcynis catulina]]'', ''[[Carcharhiniformes|Palaeoscyllium formosum]]'', ''[[Paracestracion|Paracestracion falcifer]]'', and ''[[Macrourogaleus|Macrourogaleus hassei]]''.{{cite journal |last=Thies |first=D. |date=1995 |title=Placoid scales (Chondrichthyes: Elasmobranchii) from the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian) of northern Germany |journal=Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology |volume=15 |issue=3 |pages=463–481 |doi=10.1080/02724634.1995.10011242 |bibcode=1995JVPal..15..463T }} ==Notes== {{notelist}} ==References== {{Reflist|}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q141658054}} [[Category:Enigmatic fish taxa]] [[Category:Taxa named by Tyler Greenfield]] [[Category:Fossil taxa described in 2026]] [[Category:Elasmobranchii]] [[Category:Prehistoric cartilaginous fish genera]]
